oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: latency_p99_spike on inference-serving-prod (region: us-west-2). p99 increased from 380ms -> 3.2s over last 5m. SLO breached. Alert ID: INC-20260314-01

oncall-bot: Affected routes: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/generate (mostly streaming responses). Error rate stable, but streaming stalls and token emit gaps observed.

maria_chen: seeing same in dashboard — p95 ~ 420ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~ 3.2s. tail_latency spike aligns with high KV cache eviction_rate.

jamal: good catch. any recent infra or runtime deploys in last hour?

luca: I rolled out runtime v2.13.4 to canary ~45m ago (kernel selection change + kv-cache tuning). Not pushed cluster-wide yet.

maria_chen: okay — let's check kv cache metrics. tagging infra-alert for cache owners @infra-alert

infra-alert: KV cache metrics: total_entries by shard spiking, eviction_rate spike at 22:03 UTC, fragmentation ratio high (~0.67). prefill_hits low vs decode_hits high. Means prefill filling a lot then being evicted before decode can reuse.

eva_ops: logs show repeated messages: "kv_cache: evicting key=<model:aurora-v1:ctx:...> reason=memory_pressure" and "task:streaming stall at token_emit, waiting for KV fill"

maria_chen: that matches "prefill vs decode imbalance" — prefill side is producing many prefix entries placing pressure, decode threads then starve or wait, causing streaming stalls and tail latency.

jamal: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) temporarily reduce prefill concurrency 2) increase kv_cache quota on hot pools 3) enable fallback to smaller model variant with smaller KV footprint 4) throttle bursty clients via rate limit rules. Which can we do fastest?

luca: I can flip an experiment flag to set prefill_concurrency=1 for prod in ~2min (config push). That should reduce prefill pressure. Also we can bump KV cache size on pool-3 by +30% — needs infra approval but quick scale should be fine.

eva_ops: I'll open a scaling op: "scale kv-cache-pool-3 +2 nodes" — running kubectl scale statefulset/kv-cache-pool-3 --replicas=5. command queued.

maria_chen: good. Also add an emergency routing rule: route streaming traffic for the largest customers to model-aurora-quantized-small which has smaller KV working set. Can we do that with runtime routing?

luca: yes — I can add a routing override for 15m window: set policy route(streaming) if customer in {enterprise-ids} -> model=aurora-v1-small. Pushing now.

jamal: while infra scales, please collect a short diagnostic payload: run internal endpoint /internal/kv/stats and paste top 5 shards by eviction_rate and their mem_pressure.

eva_ops: output from /internal/kv/stats (sanitized):
```
shard-3: eviction_rate=124/s, mem_used=78GB, mem_limit=80GB, fragmentation=0.68
shard-7: eviction_rate=98/s, mem_used=65GB, mem_limit=70GB, fragmentation=0.59
shard-1: eviction_rate=12/s, mem_used=21GB, mem_limit=64GB, fragmentation=0.12
... 
```

maria_chen: shard-3 is the hot one. Looks like one model variant pinned hot on that shard. Any idea why fragmentation is so high?

luca: could be variable-sized KV entries (longer past context) + uneven shard assignment. Also our allocator doesn't coalesce freed slots aggressively; we've seen fragmentation when eviction churn is high.

jamal: next steps: 1) scale pool to relieve mem pressure (in progress) 2) flip prefill_concurrency=1 (luca) 3) temporarily reduce max_prefix_length for streaming requests to cut average entry size 4) schedule a low-impact rolling restart of kv-cache pods to defragment in controlled manner 5) long-term: implement compacting allocator / migrate to slab allocator.

eva_ops: scale command succeeded — new replicas becoming ready (3 -> 5). Memory pressure dropping on shard-3: mem_used=62GB now. eviction_rate trending down.

maria_chen: p95 back to ~420ms, p99 dropping to ~1.3s. still higher than target but improving. Good.

luca: prefill flag toggled to 1. That reduced prefill burst by ~60% per traces.

jamal: we should also notify product/CS for impacted customers and log incident on status page if external SLA affected. Any customers seeing errors?

eva_ops: no 5xx spike; mostly increased latency for streaming. CS inbox flagged three slow sessions, reaching out.

maria_chen: I'll draft a short customer note: "We observed elevated streaming latency in us-west-2. Mitigations applied; p99 improved. No increases in error rate. We'll post updates if degradation persists."

jamal: handing off to night oncall — @luca, you'll be primary for follow-ups? If anything re-escalate to eng-runtime and infra.

luca: on it. I'll monitor for next 60m and run rolling restarts on remaining shards after low-traffic window. If p99 > 2s for >10m, page eng-runtime.

eva_ops: logging actions taken: scale pool, toggle prefill_concurrency, routing override to smaller model, reduce prefix length, started rolling restart plan (staggered 1 pod every 5m).

maria_chen: final metrics snapshot (post-mitigations): p95=410ms, p99=920ms, eviction_rate global down 80%, fragmentation slowly decreasing. Marking incident as mitigated but not resolved.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260314-01 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Owner: luca. SLA impact: partial (latency). Next update scheduled in 30m.

jamal: thanks team. Add follow-up action items to eng-runtime backlog: compacting allocator, shard rebalancer, prefill heuristics tied to shard mem pressure, and improved alerting for kv-fragmentation.

luca: noted. will create RFC and link to this thread.

maria_chen: handing off to @luca for overnight. I'll update the incident ticket with customer notes. ttyl."
